alternativas.feedback: Correto. This electron micrograph shows a cell whose cytoplasm contains numerous lipid droplets. Lipid droplets are bounded by a single layer of phospholipids, not a unit membrane. The monolayer is coated with proteins that provide structural integrity, regulate lipid metabolism and facilitate droplet docking with other organelles. Lipids droplets often coalesce with each other. 6000x

Correto. The epithelial cells lining the oviduct, seen here, possess numerous small lipid droplets in their apical cytoplasm. This tissue has been fixed with osmium tetroxide, which stabilizes the lipid, preventing it from being extracted by fat solvents used during tissue processing. This reaction of osmium with lipid results in a yellowish-brown product that is visible by light microscopy. Toluidine blue stain, 1000x

camada.alt: Camada de marcação sobreposta à lâmina, apontando a estrutura que a questão pede.

alternativas.feedback: Correto. In specialized lipid storage cells (adipocytes), a single, large droplet nearly fills the entire cell, with only a thin rim of cytoplasm around it. This image shows a small accumulation of adipocytes in loose connective tissue. The tissue has been fixed with osmium tetroxide, which preserves the large lipid droplet in the cytoplasm and provides the brown-black staining of the lipid. The lipid in these vesicles consists of triglycerides and cholesterol esters. Toluidine blue stain. 1000x

alternativas.feedback: Correto. Adipocytes can also form an entire tissue, as seen in this section of subcutaneous tissue beneath the skin. The “honeycomb” appearance of the tissue results from the loss of the lipid from the cells during tissue processing. In life, these cells contain a single, large droplet of lipid which nearly fills the cell and displaces the cytoplasm and nucleus to the periphery. Hypodermis 400x
